subject: Control plane / Data plane acceptance readout — Private VPC deployment
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: David Li <david.li@acme.net>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private VPC — control plane / data plane acceptance readout

Hi David / Acme infra team,

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. Attached is the consolidated reference diagram we used in the smoke testing: vpc-reference-diagram.pdf (PDF, 2.1MB).

For the acceptance readout today we covered the following items and I wanted to capture outcomes and remaining action items:
- Control plane connectivity: API endpoints reachable from ACME mgmt subnets (verified)
- Data plane egress: inference nodes can reach external artifact storage via NAT (partial; intermittent during high TCP resets)
- Service discovery: internal SRV records for edge-proxy(s) validated
- Certificate rotation: short window tested, keys stored in Acme KMS demo account

Can you confirm the temporary behavior on the NAT resets (line-item 2) and share the final egress-IP list we should allow (we will add to our egress ACL template)?

Next steps I propose:
1) You send final egress-IP CSV and any iptables/NAT notes by EOD Wed (Aug 11)
2) We run one more 30-minute load run targeting 80 QPS on Thu (Aug 12)
3) If green, schedule cutover window Fri (Aug 13) 02:00-06:00 UTC

If any of the above windows don't work for you, propose alternatives.

Thanks,
Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132
Redwood Inference
From: David Li <david.li@acme.net>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Infra Team <infra@acme.net>, Rachel Porter <rporter@acme.net>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC — control plane / data plane acceptance readout

Jonas — thanks for the summary and the diagram. Short answers below and an update on the NAT resets:

- NAT resets: during the first run we saw a small cluster of reset events originating from a misconfigured TCP keepalive on the upstream NAT appliance (vendor image v2.7.1). We pushed a patch to the NAT image to increase the keepalive and reduced aggressive connection pruning. After the patch, resets dropped to <0.01% of connections during a sustained 60-minute run.

- Egress IPs: attached is the current export (redwood-egress-ip-list.csv). There are 7 public NAT IPs fronting the data plane. We recommend adding all seven to your outbound ACL for a minimum viable cutover.

- Cert rotation: confirmed — KMS integration performed in staging; production KMS ARN will be provided in a separate secure note.

We can do the 80 QPS run on Thu (2026-08-12) at 16:00 UTC. Cutover window noted; Fri 02:00-06:00 UTC works for our on-call.

Attaching: redwood-egress-ip-list.csv (CSV, 1KB)

—David

David Li
Principal Infra Engineer, Acme Corp
david.li@acme.net
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, David Li <david.li@acme.net>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 12:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC — control plane / data plane acceptance readout

Thanks David — great catch on the NAT image. Two operational/security items I want to lock down before we call the deploy green:

1) Egress filtering & monitoring: please confirm that Acme's NAT pool has stable BGP advertisements for the seven IPs and that the signal will not be moved during the cutover. If there is any scheduled maintenance in the 72h window, flag it now.

2) Audit logs & retention: our compliance team requires token-level audit logs for 90 days for any production tenant mapping. Can Acme confirm retention and the S3-compatible endpoint (we'll need the bucket path and IAM role mapping)? If you prefer, we can provide a short template (soc2-ports-and-hosts.xlsx) to map ports/protocols and retention fields.

3) TLS mutual auth: edge-to-control-plane connections should present client certs; we validated rotation in staging but want production CA/chain to be shared.

If those three are satisfied, I am comfortable proceeding to the 80 QPS run.

Kimberly Park
Head of Trust & Safety Operations, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
From: David Li <david.li@acme.net>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Infra Team <infra@acme.net>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 08:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC — control plane / data plane acceptance readout

Kimberly — answered inline below: 

1) BGP/Stable IPs: confirmed. The 7 NAT IPs are announced from our transit fabric and there is no planned movement during Aug 10–15. I added a note to our maintenance calendar.

2) Audit logs & retention: we will expose a read-only S3 bucket at s3://acme-redwood-audits with 90-day lifecycle. IAM role details to follow via encrypted ticket (INFRA-9142). Attached is a minimal mapping spreadsheet to speed your compliance onboarding (soc2-ports-and-hosts.xlsx).

3) TLS mTLS chain: production CA chain will be uploaded to the drive link you shared; we will notify when complete.

Also — one small ask: during the Thu load run please exercise the long-sequence token path (4k tokens) for a subset of requests so we can validate KV cache behavior under NAT churn.

Thanks,
David
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: David Li <david.li@acme.net>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2026 09:50:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC — control plane / data plane acceptance readout

Thanks all — quick acceptance summary and operational checklist before the Thu run at 16:00 UTC: 

A. Preconditions (ALL satisfied):
- NAT keepalive patch deployed; resets reduced (David)
- Egress IP list received and announced (redwood-egress-ip-list.csv)
- KMS and mTLS chain pending final upload (expected Wed EOD)
- Audit log S3 path and retention confirmed (INFRA-9142)

B. Run plan (Thu 16:00 UTC):
- 30 minutes ramp to 80 QPS, hold for 30 minutes, then 30 minute soak at 80 QPS
- Exercise 20% of requests with 4k token sequences to validate KV cache paths (David's ask)
- Observability: token-level latency, per-IP error heatmap, NAT connection churn. Dashboards: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD-example-vpc-materials

C. Rollout (if green):
- Cutover Fri 02:00-06:00 UTC; brief 10m validation windows every hour
- On-call rotation: Acme on-call during cutover hour 1; Redwood rotates to ops team after hour 2

Action items:
- David: upload KMS ARN + CA chain to drive by Wed 18:00 UTC
- Kimberly: share compliance mapping (you already attached the spreadsheet) — we will fill and return by Wed EOD
- Irene / Stephanie: I will run the load plan and share a post-run telemetry snapshot within 1 hour of completion

Jonas

--
Jonas Weber
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: David Li <david.li@acme.net>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Infra Team <infra@acme.net>, Rachel Porter <rporter@acme.net>
Date: Thu, 12 Aug 2026 16:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private VPC — control plane / data plane acceptance readout

Jonas / team — sign-off from Acme side. The Thu load run completed as planned: no regressions in token latency, NAT churn within expected thresholds, and KV cache behavior looked stable during the 4k token subset.

We uploaded the production CA chain and KMS ARN to the drive link (same folder) and confirmed S3 bucket permissions for the audit role. Maintenance calendar updated; no conflicts for Fri cutover.

We are ready to proceed with the cutover window. Please share the final cutover-runbook and on-call rotation before 22:00 UTC.

—David

David Li
Principal Infra Engineer, Acme Corp
